main_text.p: ex parte uanifsimæ compe-riebantur,pofita erat,populus Romanus quafi ad ocio-fos homines pertinentem,fe rè reliquit: eum ipfum, quē diximus, Socratē fapientif-fimum Apollinis oraculo iu dicatū imitatus, qui rerum naturaliū inquifitionem ob-fcuram ( ut Cicero teftatur) & ad bene uiuendum non neceffariam,omifit: philofo Phiamque deuocauit è cœ-lo, & in urbibus collocauit, &in domos etiam introdu-xit.Moralem autem, quę re-uera hoc erat digna nomine, hoc eft, non ad uanas quafdā & inanes uerborum concer-ta-

page.notes: The running head is a solid dark bar in print, with no legible words, so it is marked illegible. The large "P" at the start of "Phiamque" is a drop capital from "philosophiamque", split across the line end after "philofo". No marginal notes or catchword on this page. The text runs on from the previous page and ends mid-word at "concer-ta-", so the last word is continued on the next page.
